$corrections: MARA: Mike said 23,000 BTC for $1.7-1.8B. Actual per the 10-Q filed 2026-08-06: 23,093 BTC for ~$1.63B across H1 2026 at an average of $70,631. Corrected everywhere.

200-week SMA: Mike framed a close below it as a future risk. It ALREADY happened in late June 2026 ($59,486 weekly close vs a $62,443 200-week SMA), the first since June 2022. Reframed as already broken, reclaimed, and now retested from below by a rising average. This is the stronger and the correct framing.

Layoffs: Mike said July was the lowest layoff month since 2022. Challenger July 2026 was 33,429, a TWO year low. 'Since 2022' actually belongs to the HIRING plans line (16,095, best July since 2022). Both stated correctly.

Louie the duck: name is Louie not Louis; token first pool 2026-08-08 (two days before the stream, not three); the 6 million views in 24 hours figure is unverifiable and is NOT asserted. What IS asserted is the verified outcome: $LOUIE is down about 74% in 24 hours at roughly a $100K market cap, which vindicates Mike's on-stream call.

DROPPED the Kitsu and Cooper tweet. The claim that Kitsu is Vlad Tenev's dog and Cooper is the Robinhood office dog traces only to the tokens' own marketing sites, which themselves disclaim any Robinhood or Tenev relationship. Persona rule verified_claims_only. Cooper's market cap is also about $88K, which is noise.
DROPPED the Swapy tweet: no token by that name exists on Robinhood Chain per DEX Screener. Likely a mishear of $POOLS.
TUT deliberately excluded: it is down about 74% from its 2026-08-09 ATH and the angle is already queued three times from yesterday's batch.

yt_posts.body:
Michael Saylor's favorite Bitcoin stat is that it has traded above its 200-week SMA about 92% of the time, by his own math. It is the line his whole thesis leans on. Here is the part that does not make the highlight reel: Bitcoin already lost that line this year, and it is sitting right back on it today.

Late June, Bitcoin closed a week at $59,486 with the 200-week SMA at $62,443. That was its first weekly close beneath that line since the 2022-23 bear market. It clawed back above, and everybody moved on.

The problem is that the average keeps climbing, about $200 every single week, because the sub $20,000 weeks from late 2022 keep rolling out the back of the four year window. It was $62,443 in June. It is near $64,000 now. Bitcoin is around $63,600, which puts it a hair under the line as I write this: it closed above the average last week and has slipped back beneath it since. You do not need a crash to lose this line. You just need another week of nothing, because the line is the thing that is moving.

Now stack what is sitting on top of that.

Supply. MARA sold 23,093 Bitcoin in the first half of this year at an average price of $70,631. That is $1.63 billion of coins moving out of a miner's treasury and back into the market. Their stack went from 53,822 down to 35,577, and only 26,307 of what is left is unrestricted; the rest is loaned out or pledged as collateral.

Jobs. July had 33,429 announced layoffs, a two year low, and hiring plans were the strongest for any July since 2022. Sounds great. Payrolls still printed negative 23,000 against 80,000 expected, with May and June revised down a combined 103,000. Nobody is firing. Nobody is hiring. The whole thing froze in place.

Inflation. CPI came in exactly in line this morning, 3.4% headline and 2.5% core, easing from 3.5% in June. No relief and no shock, which means the week gets decided by PPI on Thursday and retail sales on Friday.

And on the fun side of the market, only 37% of traders across the Robinhood chain's top 50 tokens are in profit. Everybody is spreading the same money across twenty tickets instead of five, so every pump lands smaller than the last one.

Any one of these on its own is noise. Stacked together, they are why I am building dry powder instead of chasing green candles.

I also finally pushed the Johnny Cash button on stream this week, so if it all goes red you know exactly who to blame.

Does Bitcoin hold the 200-week SMA into September, or lose it again? Tell me which one in the comments. And hit like and subscribe if you would rather be early on the next setup than read about it afterwards.

$post_run_corrections: 2026-08-12, after the run: a frame of Mike's own TradingView (stream at 2026-08-10) read 'SMA 1W 200 close 62,034' against BTCUSD 63,956, which looked like it contradicted the ~$63,770 / under-1% figures in this plan. A second verification pass reproduced the published 200-week SMA series from raw Bitstamp and Kraken price history and matched the reported values to within $1-$8, proving the screenshot was a stale crosshair reading of the June 8 bar, not a live value. The under-1% gap was CORRECT.

That pass did surface two REAL errors, now fixed in both this plan and the queued entries: (1) 'first weekly close below since June 2022' is wrong, there were weekly closes below the 200-week SMA through October 2023, so it is now 'since the 2022-23 bear market'; (2) the levels moved, so the copy now reads BTC about $63,600 against a 200-week SMA near $64,000, and adds the mechanism (the average climbs about $200 a week as sub $20K weeks from late 2022 roll out of the four year window).
The Saylor 92% figure is ATTRIBUTED, never stated as bare fact: an independent replication on Kraken weekly closes gives 89.2%, so it is his number computed his way.
